topic: Fourier-separated honest inference for partial-order Cholesky effect fibers. Fix dimension p, treatment T, outcome Y, known strict partial order P, confidence level alpha, spectral bounds 0<lambda<Lambda, envelope constants 0<c<C, known finite ray exponents q_u bounded by Q on coordinate and pair-sum rays, and E||X||^8<=M8. Observe iid X=U+G_Gamma, where G_Gamma is independent centered Gaussian, lambda I<=Gamma<=Lambda I is the greatest Gaussian-divisor covariance, and U is generated by finitely many independent nonconstant Gaussian-indecomposable sources with bounded loadings and c(1+|t|)^(-q_u)<=|phi_U(tu)|<=C(1+|t|)^(-q_u) for |t|>=1. Construct explicit measurable finite-sample simultaneous ray and covariance regions using centered empirical characteristic-function moduli, polarization, spectral clipping, and a bounded fallback. Enumerate predecessor ideals and return the union of covariance-region images for the full compatible total-effect fiber Theta_TY(Gamma,P); prove uniform whole-fiber coverage and O(1/log N) excess radius and expected Hausdorff error, including exact effect-collision strata without a swap margin. On the explicit exponent-two three-variable subclass with fixed common envelope constants and sufficiently generous fixed eighth moment containing the smooth Laplace--Student splice, prove matching logarithmic covariance, singleton-effect, and honest-confidence diameter lower bounds along Gamma(s)=Gamma1+s aaT. For literal standardized-Laplace sources with loadings bounded away from zero, prove root-N recovery by fourth cumulants as a parametric boundary. Credit Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi for mixed-noise finite identification, Meister (2006) for scalar fixed-envelope centering and lower pairs, and Belomestny--Trabs--Tsybakov (2019) for multivariate polarization. CRAN pcalg::ida and the Maathuis et al. yeast intervention-ranking workflow are the consumer: under an audited mixed-noise/Fourier model, report an honest compatible-effect set rather than a selected Gaussian-causal-sufficiency list. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: Derived simultaneous finite-sample covariance regions, whole-fiber coverage, and O(1/log N) expected Hausdorff error. The lower splice fits an explicit class with p=3, lambda=1/10, Lambda=4, c=2/5, C=60, exponent two, eighth moment at most 50000000, and reduced loading norm at most three; its zero polynomial moments give exact eighth-moment accounting. Embedding a=(1,2/5,1) along Gamma(s)=Gamma1+s aaT keeps the equality-stratum effect equal to (3/5+s)/(1+s), giving the causal lower pair. Checks covered 577 legal orders, divisor status, empirical zeros, collision strata, positive definiteness, and the literal-Laplace cumulant boundary; direct donor comparisons found no same whole-fiber theorem. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Independently verify the uniform Fourier-derivative and weighted-Plancherel estimates in Lemmas 7--8 for m=6 and the displayed cutoff, including their uniform constants. EARLY KILL TEST: Recheck that the m=6 smooth splice stays positive, satisfies the common envelopes and fixed eighth moment, and has vanishing product-experiment divergence; failure invalidates the matching lower claim. open_problems.open_problem: Construct a margin-free finite-sample confidence region that simultaneously covers the full partial-order-compatible total-effect fiber when the causal covariance is an unknown greatest Gaussian divisor.

source_refs.claim: The paper establishes unique identification with known causal structure and finite identification with unknown structure, but does not provide uncertainty quantification.
source_refs.author: Vahideh Sanjaroonpouri and Pouria Ramazi

source_refs.claim: The paper derives nonasymptotic characteristic-function estimators and logarithmic rates for a latent Gaussian covariance, without mapping covariance uncertainty into causal-effect fibers.
source_refs.author: Denis Belomestny, Mathias Trabs, and Alexandre B. Tsybakov

source_refs.claim: The paper uses test inversion to cover causal effects under structure uncertainty and highlights nonsmoothness, but assumes an equal-error-variance model.
source_refs.author: David Strieder and Mathias Drton

open_problems.why_unsolved: Prior work ends at three distinct boundaries: mixed-noise SCM results give finite population identification, IDA-style methods enumerate plug-in effect values, and existing structure-uncertainty confidence regions assume a different identifiable model. The prior CausalSmith fiber construction obtains coverage by projecting a directly observed Gaussian covariance region and explicitly leaves non-Gaussian positive inference outside its scope. Here the first missing proof step is a simultaneous centered empirical-characteristic-function modulus bound that remains valid after coordinate/pair-sum polarization, empirical zeros, and spectral clipping. That covariance region must then be mapped through every compatible Cholesky regression without selecting an ordering or imposing separation at exact effect collisions.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A theorem specifying an explicit measurable ray-based covariance region and the union of its partial-order-compatible Cholesky-effect images, with uniform level-(1-alpha) whole-fiber coverage and an expected Hausdorff-radius bound valid on collision strata.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation treats numerical effect uncertainty and uncertainty over causal structures as one inferential object.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Classical effect intervals condition on a known graph -> observational data leave several structures compatible -> learn-then-infer omits structural uncertainty -> cover every mixed-noise effect compatible with the supplied partial order

method_exemplars.technique: Use log empirical characteristic-function moduli at coordinate and pair-sum frequencies, polarization, and concentration inequalities to recover a latent Gaussian covariance.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its target is precisely a Gaussian covariance hidden by independent nonparametric contamination; the new work must turn its point estimator bounds into a simultaneous region and propagate that region to a set-valued causal target.

method_exemplars.technique: Enumerate possible parent sets under background knowledge and evaluate adjustment-based total-effect functionals for each retained structure.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A strict partial order restricts admissible DAGs, and the requested fiber is the population set of the resulting Cholesky-effect functionals.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert goodness-of-fit tests for causal orderings and propagate the retained ordering set into causal-effect confidence regions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides the nearest confidence-set architecture for retaining multiple causal orders, although its tests must be replaced by finite-sample Fourier-divisor regions.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish the sharp minimax Hausdorff risk and honest confidence-set diameter for partial-order Cholesky effect fibers under unknown Gaussian-divisor covariance, including least-favorable alternatives on exact effect-collision strata.

source_refs.claim: The paper proves matching logarithmic minimax rates for latent Gaussian covariance estimation using Fourier-domain least-favorable alternatives.
source_refs.author: Denis Belomestny, Mathias Trabs, and Alexandre B. Tsybakov

source_refs.claim: The paper proves a constant-over-log-n minimax lower bound for pointwise signal-density estimation with centered Gaussian noise of unknown variance.
source_refs.author: Catherine Matias

source_refs.claim: The paper identifies nonsmooth total effects under structure uncertainty as an inferential obstacle but does not derive mixed-noise minimax diameter bounds.
source_refs.author: David Strieder and Mathias Drton

derive the limiting minimax correct-certification envelope beta*(c)

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing least-favorable constructions separate a scalar Gaussian noise level or a latent covariance matrix, not the set-valued image of multiple Cholesky regression maps. A covariance perturbation may be annihilated by the relevant regression functional or may only permute fiber elements that already coincide, so a covariance lower bound does not automatically imply Hausdorff or confidence-diameter separation. Prior proposal reviews separately identify the unresolved local branch-cone minimax envelope. The first required step is an explicit positive-definite covariance path and compatible source perturbation whose product-experiment divergence stays bounded while a designated total effect changes at logarithmic order; the local limit must then account for distinct branch derivatives at an equality stratum.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Matching upper and lower theorems for covariance, singleton-effect, fiber-Hausdorff, and honest-confidence diameter loss, together with an explicit least-favorable collision submodel and the minimax rule for its limiting union-of-cones experiment.

writing_exemplar.why: Its progression from spectral estimator through oracle bounds to a matching testing construction is the closest narrative for a sharp causal-functional minimax result.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Unknown contamination makes Gaussian covariance recovery severely ill-posed -> Fourier estimators attain logarithmic error -> least-favorable noise mimics covariance perturbations -> determine whether the same information bound governs the compatible causal-effect fiber

method_exemplars.technique: Modify nuisance characteristic functions over a high-frequency transition band and bound chi-square divergence between covariance alternatives.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested causal lower pair needs the same Fourier-mimicry construction, augmented by a covariance direction with nonzero Cholesky-effect separation.

method_exemplars.technique: Replace smooth local asymptotics by projection onto tangent cones and derive the corresponding constrained Gaussian limit experiment.
method_exemplars.why_closest: At an effect collision, the local fiber is indexed by branch-specific tangent cones rather than one differentiable parameter map.

method_exemplars.technique: Invert hypotheses about a nonsmooth total-effect functional while retaining every compatible causal structure.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its set-valued treatment of structure uncertainty supplies the causal loss and coverage architecture to which the Fourier lower pair must be transferred.

open_problems.open_problem: Characterize and adapt to the transition from logarithmic Fourier recovery to root-N fourth-cumulant recovery of Gaussian-divisor covariance and compatible effects as Laplace loading and cumulant separation shrink.

source_refs.claim: The paper derives estimating equations and asymptotic distributions for fourth-moment ICA procedures including FOBI, JADE, and FastICA.
source_refs.author: Jari Miettinen, Sara Taskinen, Klaus Nordhausen, and Hannu Oja

source_refs.claim: The paper identifies linear SCMs containing Gaussian noise under Gaussian-indecomposable confounding, but does not establish a cumulant-based root-N inferential boundary.
source_refs.author: Vahideh Sanjaroonpouri and Pouria Ramazi

source_refs.claim: The paper establishes logarithmic minimax covariance rates over broad nonparametric contamination classes, providing the slow side of the proposed boundary.
source_refs.author: Denis Belomestny, Mathias Trabs, and Alexandre B. Tsybakov

leaving only the small-m frontier open.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Fourth cumulants eliminate independent Gaussian components, and standardized Laplace sources have known nonzero kurtosis, suggesting a finite-dimensional tensor route absent from the ordinary-smooth envelope class. Uniform root-N inference nevertheless requires quantitative uniqueness of the cumulant decomposition, alignment of source symmetries with the partial order, and stable propagation to every compatible effect. These properties degenerate when loadings or kurtoses shrink or tensor components coalesce. The prior proposal explicitly leaves the shrinking-separation phase diagram and adaptive switching unresolved; naive pretesting between cumulant and Fourier estimators can under-cover in the transition zone.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A data-driven hybrid covariance and effect-fiber confidence procedure with uniform coverage, a joint root-N limit law on an explicitly cumulant-separated Laplace subclass, logarithmic risk on the wider Fourier class, and matching lower bounds throughout a stated shrinking-separation phase diagram.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames mixed Gaussian/non-Gaussian causal models through the contrast between Gaussian nonidentifiability and recovery under Gaussian-indecomposable sources.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Gaussian components obscure linear causal structure -> indecomposable non-Gaussian sources restore population identification -> generic Fourier separation remains statistically slow -> locate and adapt to the Laplace-cumulant regime where root-N inference becomes possible

method_exemplars.technique: Jointly diagonalize fourth-cumulant matrices and linearize their estimating equations to derive asymptotic laws for a recovered mixing transformation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The fast regime relies on the same Gaussian-annihilating fourth-cumulant tensor, followed by a delta method for divisor covariance and causal-effect maps.

method_exemplars.technique: Resolve ICA permutation and scaling ambiguities using linear-SEM normalization and acyclic ordering constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The cumulant decomposition identifies directions only up to ICA symmetries, which must be reconciled with the supplied partial order before effects can be reported.

method_exemplars.technique: Prove logarithmic lower bounds using Fourier-domain alternatives whose nuisance component mimics a Gaussian covariance shift.
method_exemplars.why_closest: These alternatives define the slow comparison class and can test whether root-N recovery remains honest as cumulant separation disappears.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether Fourier cutoffs and simultaneous ray thresholds can be chosen data-adaptively when ordinary-smooth exponents and envelope parameters are unknown while retaining honest coverage of the induced total-effect fiber.

source_refs.claim: After obtaining logarithmic minimax covariance rates, the paper explicitly leaves data-driven adaptation to unknown tuning parameters open.
source_refs.author: Denis Belomestny, Mathias Trabs, and Alexandre B. Tsybakov

source_refs.claim: The paper shows that unrestricted unknown Gaussian error variance prevents uniform consistency, whereas compact variance restrictions restore it under nonparametric smoothness conditions.
source_refs.author: Alexander Meister

source_refs.claim: The paper constructs bootstrap uniform deconvolution bands with unknown ordinary-smooth error distribution, but uses an auxiliary error sample.
source_refs.author: Kengo Kato and Yuya Sasaki

open_problems.why_unsolved: The oracle cutoff balances exponential attenuation from the unknown Gaussian covariance against polynomial decay of source characteristic functions, so the ray exponent and envelope enter both stochastic amplification and bias. Existing adaptive deconvolution results either know the relevant error law or have an auxiliary error sample. In this model the same empirical characteristic function must identify the Gaussian divisor, choose all ray cutoffs, and certify simultaneous coverage; data-dependent selection can therefore under-cover before polarization or Cholesky projection is attempted.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: Either an adaptive finite-sample confidence-set theorem with data-driven ray cutoffs and an oracle-rate expected Hausdorff bound over a stated union of exponent classes, or a testing lower bound showing that honest adaptation requires an explicit self-similarity or exponent-separation condition.

writing_exemplar.why: It derives the nonadaptive logarithmic benchmark and directly identifies data-driven tuning as unresolved.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Fourier attenuation determines the usable frequency -> an oracle cutoff yields logarithmic covariance recovery -> that cutoff depends on unknown decay parameters -> seek adaptive honest coverage for the resulting causal-effect fiber

method_exemplars.technique: Use Gaussian approximation and a multiplier bootstrap for the supremum of a Fourier deconvolution process with an estimated nuisance characteristic function.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The required region likewise depends on simultaneous empirical-characteristic-function errors, but must estimate the Gaussian divisor without auxiliary noise observations.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct honest sets in ill-posed models by separating concentration-controlled stochastic radius from regularization bias and bounding expected diameter.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Honest adaptive fiber inference must control cutoff bias as well as the empirical-process radius in a severely ill-posed inverse problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate an unknown Fourier-decay index and insert it into an adaptive procedure for a semiparametric convolution model.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a concrete template for learning a decay parameter before selecting Fourier regularization, although not for simultaneous causal-fiber coverage.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether distinct partial-order Cholesky total-effect maps admit output-polynomial or polynomial-delay enumeration without materializing the full predecessor-subset lattice, or prove a matching computational obstruction.

source_refs.excerpt: The algorithm still constructs an explicit 2^p subset space even when the numerical output is a singleton.
The unrestricted deterministic complexity remains open.

open_problems.why_unsolved: Fragment interning removes factorial traversal of compatible orders but still retains one state per predecessor subset, even when all completions yield one numerical effect. Related prior work shows that locally feasible effect choices need not coexist globally because downstream cancellations couple decisions. For a single treatment-outcome effect, the first proof step must change from equality of complete coefficient-row fragments to a continuation-preserving congruence based only on the rational path-sum map; it is unknown whether such a quotient can be tested without reconstructing exponentially many predecessor subsets.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An exact-once algorithm whose running time is polynomial in dimension, input bit length, and the number and encoding size of distinct effect outputs, or a hardness reduction excluding such an algorithm together with a maximal tractable class of partial orders.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates eliminating duplicate structural completions by enumerating distinct total-effect functionals directly.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Many compatible DAGs encode the same effect -> enumerating every DAG wastes computation and duplicates reports -> minimal effect-functional enumeration removes redundancy -> numerical partial-order fibers require an output-sensitive quotient beyond the subset lattice

method_exemplars.technique: Use bucket structure and acyclic-orientation moves to enumerate Markov-equivalent DAGs exactly once with bounded delay.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the nearest graph-side template for a canonical continuation rule that avoids revisiting equivalent structural completions.

method_exemplars.technique: Quotient solutions of an acyclic AND-OR graph by a local right congruence and enumerate equivalence classes with polynomial delay.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A successful Cholesky-effect enumerator likewise needs a continuation-preserving congruence, but equality of its numerical path-sum outputs may emerge only after downstream composition.

method_exemplars.technique: Prune incompatible causal orders while inverting effect restrictions into confidence regions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The enumerated maps must be evaluated repeatedly over a covariance confidence region, so canonical pruning directly controls whether whole-fiber inference is computationally usable.

literature_map:
Sanjaroonpouri and Ramazi (ICLR 2025) establish unique identification with known causal structure and finite identification with unknown structure for linear SCMs containing Gaussian noise and Gaussian-indecomposable confounders.
Shimizu et al. (JMLR 2006) provide the foundational LiNGAM contrast: independent non-Gaussian errors can resolve linear causal order where Gaussian models cannot.
Maathuis, Kalisch, and Buhlmann (Annals of Statistics 2009) introduce high-dimensional IDA, returning possible intervention effects rather than selecting a single DAG and motivating gene-ranking applications.
Perkovic, Kalisch, and Maathuis (UAI 2017) adapt IDA and adjustment to maximal PDAGs carrying background knowledge.
Fang and He (UAI 2020) provide local enumeration of possible causal effects under direct and non-ancestral background knowledge.
Strieder and Drton (Journal of Causal Inference 2023) use test inversion for total-effect regions under structure uncertainty and emphasize the nonsmooth effect map, but assume equal error variances.
Wang, Kolar, and Drton (arXiv:2305.14506) construct confidence sets for causal orderings and propagate them to causal effects.
Belomestny, Trabs, and Tsybakov (Bernoulli 2019) estimate a latent Gaussian covariance under unrestricted additive contamination using characteristic functions, obtain logarithmic minimax rates, and explicitly leave adaptive tuning open.
Meister (Statistica Sinica 2006) shows that unrestricted unknown Gaussian error variance prevents uniform recovery, while compact variance bounds and ordinary-smooth restrictions restore consistency.
Matias (ESAIM P&S 2002) and Butucea and Matias (Bernoulli 2005) provide scalar logarithmic lower bounds and least-favorable convolution constructions for unknown Gaussian or supersmooth noise scale.
Kato and Sasaki (Journal of Econometrics 2018) give multiplier-bootstrap uniform deconvolution bands with an unknown error law, but rely on auxiliary error information.
Babii (arXiv:1611.03015) develops honest confidence sets and expected-diameter control for ill-posed inverse problems.
Miettinen et al. (Statistical Science 2015) derive fourth-moment ICA estimating equations and asymptotic distributions, furnishing a plausible root-N mechanism on a separated Laplace-source subclass.
The scan found no published result combining greatest-Gaussian-divisor estimation, partial-order enumeration, whole-fiber causal coverage, exact collision strata, and matching causal-functional lower bounds; the central tension is between finite population identification, logarithmically ill-posed covariance recovery, and root-N cumulant recovery on separated subclasses.
